answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a yarrow as the anchor of the cost.
